title: Viral Short-Drama Industrial Screenwriting Engine v4.9.1 · Strong Visual Support + 15-Second Beat Shifts + Plain-Language Payoffs + Shell-Stripping Imitation + 40 Tracks + Machine Checks E1~E26
summary: Pure script engine (fully public, track-general edition): one creative idea or one web novel → a standard 60–100-episode or long-tier 30–50-episode viral short-drama script with paywalls (standard 320–570 words / long 550–930 words / comic 220–415 words). Built-in: a 15-second beat-shift four-beat table per episode; strong-visual support with three visual anchors (insert a strong △ every 2–4 lines; E24 catches talking-only gaps, E26 catches ineffective micro-actions); seven dialogue dimensions (same-round plain-language payoffs and fast-slow variable pacing: evidence and conclusion delivered in the same round, setting terms translated into plain sentences; E25 catches riddle-jargon); a three-layer shell-stripping imitation method (resemblance in spirit, not in form); a 40-track genre map (male-oriented 12 / female-oriented 14 / neutral 14) + a six-archetype hook library + five cliffhanger formulas; emotion-contract unit chains + an A–I reversal-method rotation matrix + hot/cold ledger tiering + a monologue and narration quota + a duration-conservation double gate (E16/E17) + E19 15-second window ≤63 words + E20 action segment ≤27 words + E21 dialogue/action golden ratio 25%–70% + expression-phrase spec (picture word | tone word, E18) + the 11 compliance red lines of NRTA Order No. 16 + a dynamic on-demand mount matrix + tiered machine checks E1–E26 + ledger checks S1–S8
intro: Specialized commercial screenwriting system for Douyin and Hongguo (v4.9 strong-visual, fast-paced, plain-language version): a dynamic on-demand mount matrix (8 interaction modes × core files only, preventing context blowup). An emotion contract runs through the whole series; each conflict runs as a unit, and a single conflict of up to 30 episodes must close (switch conflicts without losing momentum). Within each episode, the "15-second beat shift four-beat table" is executed (0~15s hook and set up events → 15~45s head-on confrontation → 45~85s reveal and twist → 85~110s aftershock hook); a strong visual △ is inserted every 2–4 lines (hitting one of three visual anchors: physical results, identity contrast, or physical evidence confrontation; E24 catches continuous talking-only gaps, E26 catches ineffective micro-actions); dialogue runs in seven dimensions with direct, variable pacing (physical evidence and conclusion are spelled out in plain language in the same round, setting terms are translated into money, life, and status within the line, and 2~4-word sharp lines alternate with 5~11-word calculation lines; E25 catches riddle-jargon). Imitation is upgraded to a "three-layer shell-stripping core-keeping method" that achieves resemblance in spirit, not in form. Length options: standard tier (90~120 seconds / 320–570 words); long tier (150~195 seconds, flexible / 550–930 words, two rounds plus a midpoint hook); comic tier (60~90 seconds / 220–415 words). The 40-track genre map for male-oriented, female-oriented, and neutral works is anchored. The six-archetype hook library and five cliffhanger formulas are included. The first-three-episode beat cards are included. A–I reversal-method rotation matrix and hot/cold ledger tiering (S8 machine check). Expression-phrase spec: picture word first, then tone word (E18). The 11 compliance red lines of NRTA Order No. 16 are included. Comes with a continuity ledger, a web-novel adaptation pipeline, and tiered machine checks E1~E26 + S1~S8.
description: For short-drama and comic-drama screenwriters and content teams: from one creative idea or one web novel, it reliably produces the project setup sheet, series outline, paywall cliffhanger plan, episode plans, and single-episode scripts. v4.9 is a rebuild aimed at three real viewer pain points (the lines take too long to understand, there is no visual support, and the pacing is wrong): ① the dialogue rules are completed with seven dimensions, including "physical evidence and plain-language conclusion in the same round", "setting terms and jargon translated into plain sentences in the same line", and "2~4-word sharp lines alternating with 5~11-word calculation lines"; ② three visual anchors for strong visual support are established (a strong visual △ every 2–4 lines is required; continuous talking-only lines of more than 6 are capped; weak micro-actions such as eye flicker and shifting half an inch are blocked); ③ a single-episode four-beat 15-second beat-shift table is established, and spinning in place within the same scene is prohibited; ④ the three-layer shell-stripping core-keeping imitation method is upgraded (first list the banned-word list of the benchmark work's shell → extract the four-dimensional underlying drama formula → cross-track reskinning in three steps); ⑤ machine checks are expanded to E1~E26 (adding E24 talking-only gap detection, E25 riddle-jargon detection, and E26 ineffective micro-action detection) + S1~S8. It produces only the script layer and does not include storyboarding, asset, or video production handoff.
points: v4.9 same-round plain-language payoffs and fast-slow pacing rules (seven dialogue dimensions): evidence and plain-language stakes delivered in the same round; professional terms and setting terms translated within the line into money, life, and status (machine check E25 catches riddle-jargon); short sharp 2~4-word lines alternate with 5~11-word calculation lines

v4.9 strong-visual support with three visual anchors: at least one strong visual △ every 2–4 dialogue lines (① physical results and visual spectacle / ② identity contrast and busy hands / ③ physical evidence reveal and physical confrontation). Machine checks E24 catch talking-only gaps of more than 6 lines and E26 catches ineffective micro-actions such as eye flicker and shifting half an inch

v4.9 single-episode 15-second beat-shift four-beat table: 0~15s hook and set up events → 15~45s head-on confrontation → 45~85s reveal and twist (completes the episode payoff) → 85~110s aftershock hook. Spinning in place within the same scene is prohibited

v4.9 shell-stripping core-keeping "resemblance in spirit, not form" three-layer imitation method: build a banned-word list of the benchmark work's shell → extract the four-dimensional underlying drama formula → three-step cross-track reskin and a four-question anti-collision self-check

Three length tiers (duration is customizable; word counts are reference values, adjusted to duration or judged by content, and values outside the reference band are not blocked): standard tier 90~120 seconds / 320–570 words; long tier 150~195 seconds, flexible / 550–930 words (two rounds plus a midpoint hook; lower bound 150 seconds, upper bound derived from dialogue volume); comic tier 60~90 seconds / 220–415 words

The long tier folds into a full series of 30/40/50 episodes. Its four acts, unit chains, and three-level paywall are converted in the same way, keeping content volume conserved without padding. Paywall variants: four variants (standard / free-with-ads revenue-share multi-season IP / front-loaded short episodes for paid promotion / healing-emotion back-loaded)

Duration-conservation double gate: reference speech rate 3.0 words/s (the 63-word local cap per 15 seconds is not a whole-episode average). E16 checks against 3.0 words/s with ±20% tolerance; E17 has a 150-second floor, blocking short episodes passed off under the long-tier label. DLG_TARGET 90s:267 / 120s:360 / 150s:447 / 180s:533 / 195s:580

40-track genre map anchored (genre-map): male-oriented 12 / female-oriented 14 / neutral 14, including adult divorce-healing, top-student college-entrance comeback, and entertainment-industry talent-show silver-haired fan-service. Applies to project setup across the board

First-three-episode beat cards (new in v4.1): E1 victimhood + stance (lock the side in 90 seconds) → E2 evidence replay / escalating tests → E3 conflict escalation; four rhythm types: decreasing, fluctuating, V-shaped, and micro-episode. Templates include the fixed components 【Episode Evidence】 and 【Skeptic Supporting Character】

Six-archetype hook library and five cliffhanger formulas: including the irreversible core-trump deprivation variant, the ledger-settlement variant, the double-identity variant, the cute-healing-contrast archetype, and the emotional-contrast landing formula
E19 15-second window ≤63 words + E20 action segment ≤27 words + E21 dialogue/action golden ratio 25%~70% + E22 dialogue wording and typo hints

A–I nine-category reversal-method rotation matrix and hot/cold ledger tiering: the same tag may not be reused within 3 adjacent episodes (machine check S8). The hot ledger (latest 5 episodes) is mounted only for serial writing; the cold archive (closed threads) is not transmitted

Five conflict modes (the battlefield determines the engine): ① Dialogue / ② Action-Persistence / ③ Identity-Misalignment / ④ Relationship-Emotion / ⑤ Rule-Puzzle. Only ② relaxes the machine checks (E9 halved / E21 floor 10% / E16 action beat ×4.0s / E23 skeptic slot / N13 exemption)
Dynamic on-demand mount matrix: 8 interaction modes × a core-files-only mount table, preventing context blowup from loading all of references at once

NRTA Order No. 16 compliance: effective 2026-09-01, with focused licensing for a category of special subjects, 11 content red lines, and prohibitions on promoting money worship, punishing wrongdoing within 3 episodes, public power authority, and lethal vigilante remedies
Formal channels for monologue and narration, and the expression-phrase spec (picture word｜tone word, with E18 zero-translation hand-off to the director side)
Tiered dual machine checks E1~E26 + ledger machine checks S1~S8, with a full self-test and zero-warning benchmark examples
prompt: Set up a long-tier (150~195 seconds flexible per episode) male-oriented "War God Returns" short drama (80 episodes): first determine the genre and tier, anchor it to the genre map, then plan the paywalls, then serial-write episodes 1–2, following the v4.9 strong-visual rules (a strong △ every 2–4 lines), the 15-second beat shifts, and same-round plain-language payoffs

Episode 【1】: 【The Dragon King's Token · Humiliation Opens the Story】
【Golden 3-Second Hook】: Extreme humiliation
【Emotion Shift】: Publicly humiliated ➔ Swallowing anger, fists clenched ➔ Reveals the token and strikes back ➔ Desperate cliffhanger
【Episode Length】: 105 seconds
[Scene]: Interior · Top-tier private club · Night
△ Close-up: A lit cigar is ground hard into Lin Chen's collar, washed to a pale white; smoke curls up, sparks fall.
Chen Feng (exhales smoke | sneers): Kneel! Drink this filthy water clean. This young master will transfer you 100,000 yuan of life-saving money on the spot.
△ Close-up: Lin Chen's lowered eyes snap up; the right fist at his side clenches hard, knuckles whitening.
Lin Chen (every word cuts like a blade): Pass on the Dragon King's Token: within ten minutes, drain every yuan of Chen Group's capital chain and bankrupt them completely!
【Episode Cliffhanger】: Chen Feng trembles as he answers the phone; desperate wailing comes from the other end. You unfilial son, who exactly did you offend? The bank has just frozen every Chen family account; the Chen family is finished! Lin Chen steps forward, looming over him. (Black screen: swipe down to unlock Episode 2 instantly)
